title: Enable bounded native publication for high-fanout plain Partition
question: Can automatic native publication improve competing large jobs while respecting live limits?
summary: At 1,152 files per job, competing makespan falls from 34.20 to 19.14 seconds on Linux and 22.45 to 18.41 seconds on Windows. The 192-file control misses the all-pairs gate.

workloads: Two concurrent 2 GiB snapshot Partition jobs with four configured workers and 256 MiB working budgets.

validation.summary: Sixteen integrated high-fanout runs verify semantics and cleanup. A shared-pool contract limits the rule to one writer under pressure, then restores headroom.

limitations: Both native runtimes use the same physical host. The automatic implementation reached three writer slots in the matched panel.
exclusions: Lower fanout, other pipeline shapes, browser publication, and physical device throughput.
